note: Attacker-controlled APP13 'Photoshop 3.0' segment payload (13-byte Photoshop IRB containing an IPTC record with odd data size whose data ends exactly at the buffer end) is appended to psBlob; Photoshop::valid() returns true so foundCompletePsData is set.

code: DataBuf newPsData = Photoshop::setIptcIrb(!psBlob.empty() ? psBlob.data() : nullptr, psBlob.size(), iptcData_);
note: setIptcIrb() is invoked with pPsData = psBlob.data() and sizePsData = psBlob.size() = 13, i.e. the malformed Photoshop data is processed by the vulnerable function.
First locateIptcIrb(pPsData, 13) finds the IPTC IRB at offset 0 and returns 0; sizeFront = record - pPsData = 0.

The malformed IRB's 4-byte big-endian data-size field is 1 (odd); position becomes 12 and the check dataSize > (sizePsData - position) passes because the data ends exactly at the end of the 13-byte buffer (the even-padding byte is missing).

pos is advanced to newPos(0) + sizeHdr(12) + sizeIptc(1) + (1&1)=1, i.e. pos = 14, while sizePsData is only 13. Because sizeIptc is odd and the record occupies the whole buffer, the padding term (sizeIptc & 1) pushes pos past the end; there is no check keeping pos within sizePsData.

Next loop iteration passes pPsData + 14 with sizePsData - pos = 13 - 14, which underflows (size_t wraps to a huge value), so locateIptcIrb() is called with an out-of-bounds pointer and an effectively unbounded length.

With the underflowed sizePsData the loop is entered and isIrb(pPsData + 0, 4) memcmp's 4 bytes at pPsData + 14, one byte past the end of the 13-byte Photoshop data buffer: out-of-bounds (container-overflow) read.
